about: Retrieval fixture for Lantern (ai.html). Each document is one fact per line, the shape real pasted statements, tariffs, manuals and letters have. Many documents carry competing answers to the same kind of question - several notice periods, several monthly prices, several warranty lengths - because that competition is what makes retrieval genuinely hard. Documents with a `prose` field are flowing paragraphs rather than one fact per line; they are the only entries that exercise the hard-split path inside chunkText, which has to find sentence boundaries in a wall of text.

documents.title: Guide to UK mortgage arrears and forbearance
documents.prose:
If you fall behind on your mortgage, the first thing to do is contact your lender before you miss a second payment. Lenders in the United Kingdom must follow the FCA's rules on treating customers fairly, and those rules require them to consider forbearance options before starting enforcement. Forbearance is the general term for any temporary change to your mortgage that makes payments more affordable.

The most common form of forbearance is a payment holiday, sometimes called an interest-only period, where you pay only the interest for an agreed number of months. Your balance grows during this time and your later payments rise. A second common option is a term extension, where the lender adds years to the mortgage so that each monthly payment falls. A third is a partial payment arrangement, where you pay less than the full amount for a fixed period and the shortfall is added to the balance or repaid later.

Before agreeing any arrangement the lender will ask for a full income and expenditure statement. They should give you a reasonable period to complete it and should not press you to accept the first option offered. You are entitled to seek free debt advice from StepChange, Citizens Advice or National Debtline before you sign anything, and lenders are expected to allow time for that.

Repossession is the last resort. A lender must obtain a court order before taking possession of your home, and at the hearing the court will consider whether you can realistically pay the contractual instalment plus an amount towards the arrears within a reasonable period. For a standard residential mortgage, courts have often treated two to four years as a reasonable period to clear arrears. You may ask the court to suspend a possession order, which means you keep the home as long as you keep to the payment schedule set out in the order.

If your mortgage is regulated by the FCA, which most residential mortgages are, the lender must send you an arrears notice within fifteen working days of your second missed payment, setting out the total arrears, the amount of each missed payment and a summary of your account. Ignoring that notice does not help; responding to it usually opens the conversation that leads to forbearance. Time to Pay arrangements and support for mortgage interest may be available depending on your circumstances and any benefits you receive.

documents.title: How statutory sick pay and employer obligations work
documents.prose:
Statutory sick pay is the legal minimum an employer must pay an employee who is too ill to work. It is paid from the fourth qualifying day of an absence, which means the first three days are unpaid unless the employer's own contractual scheme is more generous. The qualifying days are normally the days the employee would usually have worked.

To qualify, an employee must earn at least the lower earnings limit, currently around one hundred and twenty-three pounds per week, and must have been sick for four or more full days in a row including non-working days. Two absences within eight weeks that each last at least four days can be linked together, which matters because linked absences count towards the twenty-eight week maximum for which statutory sick pay can be paid.

Employers used to be able to reclaim some of the cost of statutory sick pay from the government, but that scheme ended in 2014, so the cost now sits with the employer. An employer must keep records of absences and payments for at least three years, and must give an employee form SSP1 within seven days of deciding they do not qualify, or at the end of a period of statutory sick pay if the employee remains off work. Form SSP1 is what the employee takes to claim employment and support allowance or universal credit instead.

An employee who is off for more than seven days needs fit note evidence, previously called a sick note, from a doctor or another qualified health professional. For absences of seven days or less an employee can self-certify. A fit note may say the employee is not fit for work, or it may say they may be fit for work with adjustments such as amended duties, altered hours or a phased return. Employers are expected to discuss those adjustments in good faith rather than treat the note as a binary yes or no.

Dismissal because of sickness can be fair if the employer follows a proper procedure, considers alternatives and obtains up to date medical evidence, but it can also amount to unfair dismissal or discrimination where the illness amounts to a disability under the Equality Act 2010. A disability is a physical or mental impairment with a substantial and long term adverse effect on normal day to day activities, and long term means the effect has lasted or is likely to last twelve months or more.

documents.title: Carbon monoxide and gas safety in rented homes
documents.prose:
Carbon monoxide is a colourless, odourless gas produced whenever a fuel such as gas, oil, coal or wood burns without enough oxygen. Because it cannot be seen or smelled, the only reliable protection is an audible alarm, and the only reliable diagnosis of an appliance problem is a qualified engineer.

Symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning closely resemble flu and food poisoning: headache, dizziness, nausea, breathlessness, collapse and loss of consciousness. The clue that points to carbon monoxide rather than illness is that the symptoms improve when you leave the building and return when you come back, and that other people or pets in the same household are affected at the same time. If you suspect carbon monoxide, open doors and windows, turn off the appliance, leave the property and call the National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999. If anyone is unwell call 999 and say you suspect carbon monoxide poisoning, because it changes how the crew will respond.

In England, landlords must have a gas safety check carried out every year by a Gas Safe registered engineer on each gas appliance and flue they provide, and must give the tenant a copy of the gas safety record before they move in or within twenty-eight days of the check. Landlords must also install a carbon monoxide alarm in any room used as living accommodation where there is a fixed combustion appliance, other than a gas cooker, and must make sure the alarm works at the start of each tenancy. Tenants should test alarms weekly and never block a flue or a ventilation brick.

Warning signs that an appliance may be burning badly include lazy yellow or orange flames instead of crisp blue ones, black sooty marks on or around the appliance, a pilot light that keeps going out, excessive condensation on windows and smoke building up in a room. None of those signs is a reason to wait; they are a reason to stop using the appliance and book an engineer. Homeowners are not legally required to have an annual gas safety check, but the same engineering logic applies and an annual service is the normal way to keep a boiler warranty valid.

documents.title: Choosing and using a heat pump in an older British house
documents.prose:
A heat pump moves heat from outside air or ground into your home rather than creating it by burning fuel, which is why it can deliver three or four units of heat for every unit of electricity it uses. That ratio is called the coefficient of performance, and it falls as the outside temperature falls, so a heat pump quoted at a coefficient of four is usually measured at a mild seven degrees outside.

Heat pumps work best at low flow temperatures, typically thirty-five to forty-five degrees Celsius to the radiators, compared with sixty-five to seventy-five degrees for a gas boiler. That means the heat emitters have to be larger, or the house has to lose less heat in the first place. In practice the single most important step before installing a heat pump in an older house is reducing its heat loss: loft insulation to around three hundred millimetres, draught sealing, and cavity or internal wall insulation where the construction allows it. A heat loss calculation, usually done room by room, tells the installer what flow temperature the system needs and whether existing radiators are big enough.

Running costs depend on the ratio between the price of electricity and the efficiency achieved. At an electricity price of around twenty-eight pence per kilowatt hour and a seasonal coefficient of performance of three, heat costs roughly nine pence per kilowatt hour of delivered heat, which is comparable to gas at seven pence. Improve the seasonal coefficient to four and heat costs fall to about seven pence per kilowatt hour. Insulating first improves that ratio more than any choice of equipment.

Planning permission is often not needed for an air source heat pump in England if it meets permitted development conditions, including limits on the size of the installation and its distance from a neighbour's boundary, but those conditions change and listed buildings and conservation areas have additional restrictions. Grants have been available to reduce the upfront cost, and the upfront cost is still several times that of a like-for-like boiler replacement, so the payback period is long unless the house has been insulated substantially first.

Noise is a common concern. An outdoor unit produces roughly forty to sixty decibels at one metre, which is comparable to a refrigerator hum to a normal conversation, and installation rules require it to be positioned so that noise at the nearest neighbour's window stays within limits. Servicing is lighter than for a boiler: an annual check of the filter, the pressure and the refrigerant circuit is normally enough, and the compressor and fan are the components most likely to need attention over a fifteen to twenty year life.
